frontMatter.title: Phase 09 evidence: plugins, browser tools and repository effects (secondary effect inventory)

summary: Phase 09 put the three families of secondary effects under the managed ceiling on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.0, git 2.54.0). Plugins: the permission broker intersects every sandboxed call's local grant with a signed plugin ceiling (plugin digest, publisher, capability, target) at the existing broker and the existing execution handlers; the ceiling may narrow consent and never mints it, never rewrites the sealed grant ledger, and a central revoke ends process, socket, media and retained service calls while a local revoke stays authoritative under it. Browser: the relay (frames, resolves and actions on a lease) and the coworking bridge hold every view, read, navigate, input, execute and clear effect against a browser ceiling by actor, effect and destination, with the actor read from the admitting transport and a navigation's admitted URL kept as the lease's provisional page. Repository: Symphony's clone, branch, fork, commit, push, pull-request, finalize and cancel are each held by themselves right before they run, in the runner and in the desktop's own IPC sinks, with the fork held inside the helper where gh repo fork happens, a denial reported as [managed-<code>] and never as an authentication failure, and no new git call on a standalone host. Deterministic coverage over the real broker, the real sealed ledger, the real policy sources, the real relay, the real coworking bridge, the real runner and the real Symphony handlers is green (71 focused files, 1645 tests). The repository family was exercised for REAL on this host: real git against a bare repository on this disk under the real repository ceiling source (eight cases: the admitted start, finalize and cancel landing commits in the bare repository with one receipt per effect; the push, the clone, a GitHub remote, a missing ceiling and the cancel each refused by name before the effect, with the bare repository untouched, the clone removed and the forge double never asked to publish). The GitHub CLI was a labeled double, so nothing was published anywhere. No ceiling was installed by an endpoint: no Mega-Maestro operation installs a plugin, browser or repository ceiling yet (CP-01, CP-03), so every enrolled desktop refuses these effects unavailable by name and every ceiling exercised here was installed by the harness over injected custody. The container run of the real sibling endpoint at this HEAD is recorded as failed-attempt evidence, answer for answer the phase 04 to 08 runs. The secondary-effects acceptance row is therefore NOT passed; every inventoried entrypoint is listed below as guarded, grant-only, no-effect or unavailable, none omitted.

failedAttemptsPreserved: The real pair run above (exit 3, every step denied or unavailable, zero leases) is kept as .maestro/playbooks/Working/09-verify/pair-run.json with the harness out/ folder under pair-20261022T230323/.

The first run of the scratch fixture test exited 1 with 3 of 8 failing: the gh double appended each call as one log line, but the PR body the runner passes is multi-line, so one 'pr create' call became six lines and the harness compared whole argument strings ('api user' against the real 'api user --jq .login'). The runner, the ceiling and git behaved correctly in that run (the admitted start, the refused push and the finalize all landed or refused as expected); only the harness's log reading was wrong. The double now folds newlines and the assertions compare the gh verb (api user, pr create, pr ready, pr edit, pr view, pr close); the rerun passed 8/8. The first run's vitest log was overwritten by the rerun, so its three assertion messages are transcribed here rather than kept as a file.

The fixture run shows ensureForkSetup reads the forge (gh api user, and gh api repos/<slug> when the user is not the owner) BEFORE the fork hold: a push refused by the ceiling still issued 'api user' to the double. These are read-only forge queries, not publications, and the fork itself is held before gh repo fork; recorded as an inventory limit rather than repaired here (reads precede the only hold that can know whether a fork is needed).

MRC-09-06 found that after an admitted navigate the relay forgot its page, so under a destinations clause every later view and input was refused destination-unknown; MRC-09-06A repaired it (the admitted URL is the lease's provisional page) and MRC-09-06B turned the parked expected failure into a plain test.

MRC-09-05 found the desktop never calls src/main/services/symphony-runner.ts (only tests import it); the real Symphony sinks are the IPC handlers, bound by MRC-09-05B and wired by MRC-09-05C. The runner keeps its gate because it is the library-side path and the one that can run over real git without Electron.

MRC-09-07 found the receipt's device actor label is lite-device:dev-1 while 'a paired Lite device (dev-1)' appears only in the unauthenticated message; and that a standalone host with a non-null source still calls ensureForkSetup with a beforeFork hook that answers null (the runner keys on gate.authority, not on standing).

Tooling: the st shell hijack ate grep, ls, cat and ranged git log, so all lookups and git calls went through node (.maestro/playbooks/Working/{g,git}.mjs) and the runner scripts under Working/09-verify/; the Bash hook refuses rm, so the scratch test was removed with fs.unlinkSync; the test type-check pattern of MRC-09-06 (a Working tsconfig extending tsconfig.main.json) was not repeated because the tsc runs above report nothing new.

deterministicCoverage.doubles: The sandbox and the plugin process (the handlers are called directly with a plugin id), the relay host (a fake request function), the coworking tool and registry entries, the fetch sink (vi.stubGlobal), the process manager behind spawnAdmitted, git and gh in the handler and runner suites (execFileNoThrow mocked), the enrolled identity (IdentityRead literals), the policy readers (closures over a mutable revision), the seal and anchor of the sealed ledger (in-memory). Everything else is real: PermissionBroker.authorize and holds, ceilingVerdict, AuthorizationStore and the sealed ledger, createPluginPolicySource / createBrowserPolicySource / createRepositoryPolicySource and their parsers, the fs.read/fs.write/net.fetch/process.spawn/net.connect/net.send handlers, pluginActBinding, admitPluginProcess, pluginHeadlessAuthority, namingSpawnLineage, BrowserRelay and registerBrowserRelayHandlers, coworkingEffectOf and holdCoworkingEffect through startCoworkingBridge, resolveTransportAdmission / transportSpawnActor / runAsTransport, ensureForkSetup with beforeFork, startContribution / finalizeContribution / cancelContribution, the symphony:start, cloneRepo, startContribution, createDraftPR, complete and cancel handlers through registerSymphonyHandlers, and the index.ts wiring assertions.
cases: Plugins, live intersection (permission-broker, authorization-ledger, plugin-policy, plugin-host-handlers): a consented in-ceiling write lands with its receipt; a consented directory, host or gateway outside the ceiling is refused by name with zero bytes, fetches or sockets; a capability the ceiling admits but the user never granted is denied with no receipt (the ceiling never mints consent); a local revoke stays authoritative under the ceiling; a re-minted plugin (new digest) is identity-mismatch at write, fetch and spawn until a ceiling names the digest, and a ceiling naming another publisher refuses again; a policy revoke of the plugin, its publisher, a withdrawn ceiling or a moved revision refuses write, fetch, spawn and the next frame of a kept socket with the sealed ledger byte-identical, enabled, not tombstoned, same epoch; standalone runs every sink on the ledger alone with no receipt whatever ceiling is installed

Plugins, act verbs and lineage (plugin-host-handlers, plugin-headless-agent-runner, tabNaming, plugin-host-deps-wiring): agents.dispatch, agents.send and agents.generateTitle hand the sink the plugin's consent-bound binding only when bound; process.spawn is admitted through admitPluginProcess on the exec-file route only; the headless runner's authority is bound per plugin; retained service calls are re-checked through holds() on every sweep so a central revoke ends them as a local one does; index.ts composes one plugin policy source and the broker reads it live

Browser (browser-policy, browser-relay, coworking-browser-bridge, coworking-lifecycle, wiring): a closed ceiling parses with limits; standalone runs every relay effect intact whatever ceiling is installed; an enrolled host with no usable ceiling is refused unavailable before any frame reaches the host; the operator is held by actor, effect and destination with each refusal never reaching the host; after an admitted navigation the next input is held against the requested page until the host reports one, back and forward leave it unknown, a refused navigation or a host failure never sets it; the actor is the admitting transport (maestro-cli, a registered paired device, an unregistered one refused unauthenticated, web login) and never the client's word; a policy revoke mid-lease ends the next frame by name; browser:createTab holds the navigation before the host is asked; the coworking bridge maps every tool call to one effect and holds it with the agent actor; index.ts composes one browser source and hands it to the relay handlers and the coworking service

Repository (repository-policy, symphony-fork, symphony-runner, symphony handlers, wiring): the parser, origins (credentials dropped, scp to ssh, local path to file:), slug and remote matching; every effect held by itself with one receipt naming the origin and never the path; clone, push, PR, finalize and cancel refused before the effect with no git or gh run and the clone removed; the fork held inside ensureForkSetup right before gh repo fork and reported as the ceiling's own message; every denial code reported as [managed-<code>] and never matching isGitHubAuthError / isGitHubMissingScopeError or login wording; the actor bound through runAsTransport; an enrolled host with no ceiling unavailable before the clone; a never-enrolled host running the chain with no managed key and no new git call; the desktop handlers holding clone, branch, fork, commit, push and pull-request (both before the push), finalize after the completing write and cancel before cleanup; index.ts composes one repository source and the bootstrap hands it to registerSymphonyHandlers
